Despite calls for AI guardrails, sadly, the Albanese Government has been "toothless" and slow to act on the threat of AI.

Actual Article Body:
The Medicare AI breach shows that Australia is currently built to respond to digital catastrophe after it happens, not to keep functioning while it is underway, writes Ben Goodsell.

DOES ANYONE BELIEVE the Australian Government has control of AI?

Anthony Albanese would like us to believe he’s in control, as he took the podium at the United Nations General Assembly to call for stronger guardrails against AI.

But our government is at best unprepared, and at worst complicit, as it lets big tech companies build data centres across our nation at lightning speed, resulting in community backlash.

The Medicare AI breach that made global headlines towards the end of September actually occurred in June.

The company responsible for the incident, OpenAI, didn’t become aware of the event until August. It failed to inform the Australian government until September, choosing to send a casual email to Services Australia.
